summary: First full E2E run of VelvetNote. Backend: 21 pytest tests run, 20 passed (95%), covering auth, catalog, admin role checks and CRUD, uploads/files, cards, Stripe checkout and webhook signature, and AI message SSE. The one failure is the brute-force lockout, which does not work behind the ingress. Frontend: the shop, personalize, Stripe and builder flows all passed. Landing CTAs, shop with 8 templates and occasion filters, Personalize (message, flip, AI writer streaming plus 'use' button, song select, envelope preview, flip to the inside, logged-out Buy -> /login?next -> back) all work. One full Stripe payment with 4242 card succeeded (/payment/success showed the title and share link; My Cards shows SENT; public /c/:slug renders with the song and the message; an invalid slug shows 'not found'). The cancel page works. In Design Studio all 6 tool tabs work: text/shape/clipart add, background color/gradient, card size, frame, the element inspector (edit, font select, duplicate/layer/delete) and dragging on the canvas. Save draft goes to /create/:id and survives a reload; the Message & Media tab fields are present; checkout reaches Stripe at $6.99. AI clipart via Gemini returned an image in about 10s and added it to the canvas. Business Studio: admin lands on /studio; customers and logged-out users are redirected. Overview stats, template publish toggle (hidden from the shop), new template (Wedding/premium, shows in the shop), template delete, asset upload/delete and the Orders table all work. The customer-facing frontend has no console errors.

critical.issue: The brute-force lockout does not work in the deployed setup. The identifier is f'{request.client.host}:{email}'. Behind the k8s ingress, request.client.host is the ingress/proxy pod IP, and it changes between requests. Failed attempts get split across several identifiers, so 5 bad passwords followed by the correct one returns 200 instead of 429. In the DB the user had count=2 on one IP after 5 failures. Fix: use the first IP from X-Forwarded-For (falling back to client.host), or key the lockout on email only.

minor.issue: Pricing can be bypassed. resolve_tier trusts kind='premade' plus any template_id from the client. A customer can send a fully custom design with kind='premade' and a classic template_id and pay $2.99 instead of $6.99. Fix: make the tier 'custom' whenever the design differs from the template, or only allow premade cards from the template design on the server.

allow_origin_regex='.*' together with allow_credentials=True reflects any origin while cookies are SameSite=None. Any site can make authenticated requests for a logged-in user. Use an explicit origin list from an env var.
Returns 200 {ok:true} even when the id does not exist. Should return 404.
No access control: anyone with the URL can fetch any upload, including voice/video. This is probably fine for share links, but worth noting.

ui_bugs.issue: Always shows 'We emailed the card link to <recipient>' when recipient_email is set, even if sending failed (the 402 insufficient credits case). It should depend on card.emailed_at / email_count.
With an empty sender, the inline inside preview signs '— You' but the dialog/viewer signs '— With love'. The two should match.
Deleting a draft has no confirmation; a single click deletes it. Premade drafts have no Edit action, only Checkout and Delete.

integration_issues.issue: Every Buy click POSTs a new card. An abandoned or cancelled checkout leaves a duplicate draft each time; My Cards collected 5+ identical 'Sunshine Get Well' drafts. Reuse the existing draft for the same template/session, or update it.

issues: The tool panel and the Message & Media panel stack first. The canvas and the Save/Buy buttons are not visible above the fold, so users have to scroll a lot to see the card they are editing.
Generated clipart has an opaque white background box that covers elements behind it on colored cards. Consider removing the background or adding a 'blend/multiply' option.
The content looks low-opacity/faded in the screenshot right after load (possibly a fade-in animation). Check that the final opacity is 1.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the login lockout identifier so it works behind the ingress (X-Forwarded-For first IP, or email-based key).
Close the tier bypass: do not trust the client's kind/template_id when the design is custom.
Restrict CORS origins (explicit list from env) since credentials are allowed.
PaymentResult: only claim 'We emailed...' when the email actually sent (emailed_at).
Avoid creating duplicate draft cards on repeated Buy clicks in Personalize.
Optional: confirm before deleting a draft; return 404 on deleting missing templates/assets; improve the mobile builder layout (canvas first).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py login(): request.client.host behind the proxy breaks the lockout (confirmed by test).
server.py resolve_tier(): the price tier comes from client-controlled fields.
server.py CORS: wildcard origin regex with credentials.
Auth playbook checks: bcrypt $2b$ hashes OK; cookies set httpOnly+Secure+SameSite=None OK; seed_admin updates the password if it changed OK; lockout FAILS; CORS not explicit.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all requested flows work; only minor UX issues)

rca of the issue: Lockout: ident = f'{request.client.host}:{email}'. Uvicorn runs without --proxy-headers / forwarded-allow-ips, so client.host is the ingress hop IP, and it varies per request (seen as 10.79.x.x). Repro: register a user, POST 5 bad logins, then the correct password returns 200 (expected 429). db.login_attempts shows several identifiers for the same email with count < 5. Mitigation: derive the IP from X-Forwarded-For[0] or lock by email.
